title: crypto/x509: mitigation for security concerns with a specific Certificate Authority
excerpt: We're blocking trust in a small set of intermediate certificates due to specific security concerns around their operation. Verify will now filter out chains which contain these intermediates, preve...
content_html:
A little context for why the release note, issue, and CL description were as vague as they were.

We were made aware of the underlying issue here yesterday (Monday), and, along with many other projects, began rushing to protect users, which due to the fractured nature of the web PKI ecosystem were likely to not all immediately receive automated trust store updates (especially those on Linux).

Our priority was two-fold, first to release a safe Go version as quickly as possible, so that we could hopefully reduce the impact for as many as users who wouldn't received automated trust store updates as possible. Secondly, we didn't want to immediately disclose the underlying issue due to the ease of exploitation. It was our expectation that the underlying issue would be publicly revealed sometime yesterday. It seems we got quite lucky that it took until a few hours ago for the underlying issue to become widely publicly known.

In the furtherance of this, we were purposefully somewhat vague as to what the security issue we were fixing was, in order to not give attackers a headstart, but attempted to convey that this was a serious issue, and that users should pick up the new release as quickly as possible. We could have likely done better here, but this is a rather uncommon event due to the widespread industry wide impact.

Reacted by Dmitri Shuralyov, Max Jonas Werner, Jordan Liggitt, William Davis, Andrew Ayer, Daniel McCarney and Youfu Zhang

Reacted by Andrew Ayer, Daniel McCarney and Alex Hamlin
